messages:
ashley: Hey all — noticed a class of broken cross-page links after the mkdocs migration. Breadcrumbs on nested pages jump to the top of the page instead of scrolling to the fragment. PR #4218 tries to normalize header IDs but a few code samples were reflowed (indentation lost). Anyone seen this? cc @priya @mike

mike: Yep, saw that in staging. Looks like the slugify plugin changed header ids (spaces -> hyphens) but our old anchors often used underscores or encoded chars. I can take a look at the slugify config. Which examples are failing?

ashley: Example: /guides/serving#kv-cache-behavior now resolves to /guides/serving#kv_cache_behavior in the mkdocs build. Also breadcrumbs on /guides/advanced/priority-queue#overview jump to top. On my branch I added a small fallback map in middleware:

```
# bad temporary hack — avoids breaking links
FALLBACK_ANCHOR_MAP = {
  "kv_cache_behavior": "kv-cache-behavior",
  "priority_queue_overview": "priority-queue-overview",
}
```

But we shouldn't ship hardcoded maps.

priya: We should avoid hardcoding. Better: add a slug-normalizer that tries both hyphen and underscore and percent-encoded variants. Docusaurus had a similar fallback we can port — it tried multiple candidate slugs before giving up.

mike: Two action items: (1) add a fallback resolver in the search-index plugin so both linkcheck and the client redirect work; (2) fix the snippet reflow — looks like mkdocs' markdown extension `strip_indent` is enabled on our build. Try toggling `preserve_whitespace` or ensure fenced codeblocks have a language tag. The indentation loss happened for code fences without a language label.

docs-bot: build #docs-staging failed: mkdocs.build: ERROR duplicate fragment id "kv-cache-behavior" (file: guides/serving.md)

ashley: Plan: remove the inline mapping, implement a small slug-normalizer util used by the link resolver, enable a non-destructive fallback chain (hyphen -> underscore -> percent-encoded), and add tests to linkcheck. Also go through the PR and add explicit language tags to code fences to prevent mkdocs from reformatting them. Timeline: small change today, follow-up cleanups tomorrow.

mike: SG. I can prototype the slugify option and a middleware that does alternate lookups on 404s. I'll open a PR against your branch so CI catches regressions.

priya: I'll add a docs-lint rule to warn when anchors are ambiguous and extend the linkcheck job with a test matrix (hyphen/underscore/encoded). Also will document the migration note for authors.

ashley: Thanks — assigning tasks: mike -> slugify + middleware; priya -> lint rule + tests; ashley -> docs fixes + PR update. I'll post the updated branch link here once it's pushed. :+1:

mike: Thanks, ping me when ready and I'll run a quick staging build.
